title: Impulse System gate
description: evaluate_impulse() in app/signals/impulse.py: GREEN / RED / BLUE from EMA(13) direction and MACD-Histogram direction together. Acts as a hard gate — RED blocks fresh BUY signals, GREEN blocks fresh SELL signals.

checklist.step: Implement direction detection for both EMA(13) and MACD-Histogram (rising/falling)
Combine into GREEN (both rising) / RED (both falling) / BLUE (disagree) per docs/Analyse.md §3
Write unit tests covering all three outputs with fixed daily OHLCV fixtures
Confirm signal-engine-orchestration actually enforces the gate (blocks/downgrades signals), not just computes the color
Run pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing and confirm no regression

decisions.decision: evaluate_impulse() computes a plain, threshold-free bar-over-bar direction for both EMA(13) and the daily MACD-Histogram (app.signals.impulse._direction: 'rising' if the latest value is strictly greater than the previous one, 'falling' otherwise -- including an exact tie). GREEN requires both directions 'rising'; RED requires both 'falling'; every other combination (a genuine disagreement between the two, or fewer than 2 daily bars to compute a direction at all) returns BLUE.
decisions.rationale: docs/Analyse.md §3 defines Green/Red purely as 'EMA(13) rising AND MACD-Histogram rising' / '...falling AND ...falling', with Blue as 'indicators disagree'. §3's own GREEN/RED/BLUE vocabulary has no third per-indicator state to represent 'unchanged' the way Screen 1's tide (§2) has a NEUTRAL state; Blue is described purely as a disagreement outcome, not an unchanged-input outcome. Considered and rejected adding an undocumented noise/flat threshold (comparable in spirit to filtering near-zero moves before calling a direction) before classifying rising/falling: the Impulse System is Elder's classic bar-by-bar color test -- comparing each new bar's indicator value directly against the prior bar's, no smoothing window -- and inventing a threshold not specified by §3 would manufacture a third per-indicator state the doc doesn't ask for. For the boundary case itself (an exact tie, latest == previous), considered and rejected treating it as 'rising' (no textual basis in §3 favors one direction over the other), and instead chose falling over rising because an indicator that hasn't advanced has not demonstrated the upward momentum GREEN requires, and this is the more conservative gate direction (a tie contributes toward blocking a fresh BUY rather than toward permitting one). Insufficient data (fewer than 2 daily bars) returns BLUE rather than raising or guessing GREEN/RED, because BLUE is the one Impulse state that doesn't gate anything ('any action allowed, weaker strength' per §3) -- the same 'don't force a guess on ambiguous/missing data' principle, adapted to the state vocabulary that actually exists here (there is no fourth 'UNKNOWN' Impulse state to invent). Correction (2026-09-12, post review of PR #10): an earlier version of this rationale and of the `_direction()` docstring in backend/app/signals/impulse.py cited a specific `app.signals.triple_screen._macd_histogram_slope` helper, a '~0.1%-of-close' flat threshold, and a screen1-tide.json decisions entry as existing precedent for the 'no threshold' choice above. None of that exists on main or in screen1-tide's own branch/task file at the time this was written -- triple_screen.py's evaluate_tide() was (and is) an unimplemented stub, and screen1-tide.json has no decisions key. That citation was fabricated rather than verified and has been removed from both this entry and the docstring; the reasoning above now stands entirely on docs/Analyse.md §3 with no cross-reference to screen1-tide's specifics.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 4 ('Confirm signal-engine-orchestration actually enforces the gate') is satisfied for this task's scope as: evaluate_impulse() computes and returns the GREEN/RED/BLUE color correctly and completely, with a docstring explicitly stating the gate-*enforcement* contract (RED blocks fresh BUY, GREEN blocks fresh SELL) that the caller must apply. Actually enforcing that gate -- i.e. having app/signals/engine.py's analyse() orchestration check the returned color before emitting a BUY/SELL signal and block/downgrade accordingly -- is out of scope for this task and was deliberately not implemented here.
decisions.rationale: docs/architecture/Backend.md §5 names app/signals/engine.py as 'the orchestration point' that 'applies the Impulse gate', and the signal-engine-orchestration task (docs/tasks/signal-engine-orchestration.json) is a separate, not-yet-started task in the task board specifically for that orchestration work -- app/signals/engine.py's analyse() is still a raise NotImplementedError stub with no dependency on impulse-system declared as an input to it yet. Considered and rejected implementing a stub enforcement helper inside impulse.py itself (e.g. a gate_signal(impulse_color, proposed_signal) function, or having evaluate_impulse() take a proposed signal and veto/downgrade it) to more literally 'confirm enforcement': that would duplicate/preempt signal-engine-orchestration's actual scope ahead of that task existing, and would be the wrong module per docs/architecture/Backend.md's module layout (§2) and §4's 'pure function' convention, which place Screen/BUY-SELL/HOLD orchestration in engine.py, not in the individual gate/indicator modules -- every other module in app/signals and app/indicators is a plain 'data in -> classification out' function with no knowledge of a 'proposed signal'. This task's own checklist item 4 is therefore addressed by verifying evaluate_impulse() is correct and its docstring states the enforcement contract (RED blocks fresh BUY, GREEN blocks fresh SELL) unambiguously for whoever implements signal-engine-orchestration next, not by building enforcement logic prematurely in the wrong module.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 4 ('Confirm signal-engine-orchestration actually enforces the gate...') is now marked done: false, reverting its earlier (incorrect) done: true.
decisions.rationale: PR #10's review flagged that item 4's literal wording ('confirm...enforces') and its done:true status disagreed with decisions[1]'s own honest text, which states enforcement was deliberately not implemented or verified because signal-engine-orchestration doesn't exist yet. Between the review's two offered fixes -- reword the checklist step's intent, or mark it not done -- marking it done: false was chosen as the more honest option: 'confirm X enforces Y' cannot truthfully be checked off when X (signal-engine.py's analyse()) doesn't exist yet to enforce anything, regardless of how reasonable the scoping decision to defer it was. Rewording the step's wording was rejected because the checklist item was authored by (and is presumably still meaningful to) whoever originally scoped this task's checklist; silently changing its stated intent risks papering over the real gap -- that gate enforcement is still unverified end-to-end -- rather than just correcting the completion status against the existing wording. This item should be revisited and closed out for real once signal-engine-orchestration exists and actually calls evaluate_impulse().
